title: The way I feel about Hell Or High Water:The Process Movie

commenti.body: this film really captures the essence of non-linear storytelling in a linear way, focusing on the characters' psychology. every scene seems to hold equal weight and can be placed anywhere without ruining the story's impact. it's a refreshing take on the heist genre, with a focus on the characters' emotions and evolving destinies.

I couldn’t make sense of your point about a non-linear film storytelling. Because we don’t have the full picture of why these two brothers are doing what they’re doing from the get-go? Because certain information is withheld from the audience until the script reveals it?

Granted, it’s been years since I’ve seen it, but from what I remember: we’re instantly introduced to these two bank robbers. As the movie goes on we realize they’re brothers, and one of them has a child to take care of while the other is on its own, has some rough priors and is ultimately unpredictable. 

Before we know “why” they’re turning to bank robbery, this additional context alone is enough to bring a sense of growing tension to the next robbery, and the next, because we understand what one of the characters has to lose, and we understand how volatile the behavior of the brother can be.

The movie reads like a modern western, and the subplot with the police – where Jeff Bridges is a reminiscent of cowboys and his partner is a descendant of Native-Americans – gives a contemporary twist to the “cowboys vs Indians” trope: they’re now working side by side, being decimated by the financial system, just like the brothers that resort to armed robbery. Old enemies work together, and what connects them to their current enemies (the “outlaws”) aren’t their differences, but their similarities. 

This is a movie that stands out as a character native but also as a genre film. It was one of the best from its year, IMO.
